en: Uh so really quickly, I think a couple things.

speaker: Drew
en: Some people will call them plugins.

en: Think when we say skills as like a unit of work.

speaker: Drew
en: It's either a workflow that you want completed or it is a policy, a standard that you want agents to adhere to.

speaker: Drew
en: That includes skills.
zh: 这就包括了技能。

speaker: Drew
en: It also includes things like hooks or MCP tools, like anything you could bundle in a plugin.

speaker: Drew
en: It's just that skills is the most popular term.
zh: 只不过技能是最流行的说法。

speaker: Drew
en: It's what everybody thinks of as the unit for agents, so we sort of use that uh interchangeably.

speaker: Drew
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Drew
en: So that's I think one.
zh: 所以我认为这是第一点。

speaker: Drew
en: The second is loops, think of these as effectively automated skills.
zh: 第二是循环，把它们想成实际上就是自动化的技能。

speaker: Drew
en: It's things that are running without immediate human intervention, at least to start them.
zh: 它们是在没有即时人工干预的情况下运行的东西，至少启动它们不需要。

speaker: Drew
en: And then as they run, typically there's some kind of meta process where the loop is uh getting better, right?
zh: 然后随着它们的运行，通常会有某种元过程，循环在其中变得更好，对吧？

speaker: Drew
en: Like as it runs, it is making things better for the next run.
zh: 就是说，随着它运行，它会让下一次运行变得更好。

speaker: Drew
en: And so you start to get compounding gains, you start to see agents sort of inflecting your productivity upwards faster than just linear.
zh: 于是你开始获得复利式的收益，你开始看到智能体让你的生产率以超过单纯线性的速度向上拐升。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: And this is like the hence the loop, right?
zh: 而这就是——所以才叫“循环”，对吧？

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: Because it goes from an agentic workflow to something that loops with some form of learning back into the beginning.
zh: 因为它从一个智能体工作流变成了某种会循环、并把某种形式的学习带回到起点的东西。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: So hopefully the second time around or the hundredth time around is better than the first one.
zh: 所以希望第二轮、或者第一百轮会比第一轮更好。

speaker: Drew
en: Right.
zh: 对。

speaker: Drew
en: Yeah, and loops are where you really start to see your first glimmers of that sort of inflection point or your trajectory really taking off.
zh: 是的，而循环正是你真正开始看到那种拐点的最初微光、或者你的轨迹真正起飞的地方。

speaker: Drew
en: And then a factory is in many ways, it's a way of working.

en: It's where you've moved almost all of your development to the creation and maintenance and monitoring of loops.
zh: 它是指你把几乎所有的开发都转移到了循环的创建、维护和监控上。

speaker: Drew
en: And the loops are now what produce most of your software or the product.
zh: 而循环现在成了产出你大部分软件或产品的东西。

speaker: Drew
en: Uh one way of thinking of this is that your factory will have some code.
zh: 呃，理解这一点的一种方式是，你的工厂会有一些代码。

speaker: Drew
en: That code will largely be loops, and then your product that you ship to users is also some code.
zh: 那些代码大部分会是循环，然后你交付给用户的产品也是一些代码。

speaker: Drew
en: Where are your humans spending their time?
zh: 你的人类把时间花在哪里？

speaker: Drew
en: When you move to the factory, you're mostly spending your time maintaining the loops uh and thinking about how to make them better.
zh: 当你转向工厂时，你大部分时间都花在维护循环上，以及思考如何让它们变得更好。

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

en: And in a way, it's like the entirety of your SDLC, right?
zh: 而在某种程度上，它就像你的整个 SDLC,对吧？

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: If your loops are kind of a kind of evolution of your pipelines, you know, of some automation that we come now.

speaker: Guy Fajani
en: So the better.

en: Yeah.

speaker: Drew
en: What have we been building?

speaker: Drew
en: So Tesla's really been trying to go on this same journey from the start of the year.
zh: 所以 Tesla 从今年年初开始就真的一直在努力走上这段相同的旅程。

speaker: Drew
en: Uh our development internally was very skills-driven to start, right?
zh: 呃，我们内部的开发一开始是非常技能驱动的，对吧？

speaker: Drew
en: We wrote down what good looks like, how we wanted code review to function, how we wanted uh if you're building something in the CLI versus in the UI, right?
zh: 我们写下了什么才是好的，我们希望代码审查如何运作，我们希望——呃——如果你是在 CLI 里构建东西，而不是在 UI 里，那会怎样，对吧？

speaker: Drew
en: Just like writing things down.
zh: 就像是把事情写下来。

speaker: Drew
en: And then once we felt like we were in a good place there, and we'll talk about why we think that's important to start there.
zh: 然后一旦我们觉得在那方面已经处于一个不错的位置——我们会谈到为什么我们认为从那里开始很重要。

speaker: Drew
en: We then wanted to really get into the business of handing work over to agents.
zh: 然后我们就想真正开始做把工作移交给智能体这件事了。

speaker: Drew
en: And so we started thinking about how we can automate more and more of our tasks so that a human isn't having to click buttons or type text into a text box to kick it off.
zh: 于是我们开始思考如何把越来越多的任务自动化，这样就不用由人来点击按钮或在文本框里输入文本来启动它。

speaker: Drew
en: Uh, and we we started that and very quickly, like the minute you get your first couple loops in place, you start to realize this is gonna get out of hand really quickly, and you have to move to a different way of working uh that has a bit more of the solution baked into the problem itself.
zh: 呃，我们开始了这件事，很快地，就在你搭好最初几个循环的那一刻，你开始意识到这会很快失控，你必须转向另一种工作方式，一种把更多解决方案直接烘焙进问题本身的方式。

speaker: Drew
en: And so that was where we made the decision like we're gonna go full factory, we're gonna build out a system where basically all of our work, all of our PRs are created by agents.
zh: 于是我们就此做出决定：我们要全面转向工厂模式，我们要建立一个系统，基本上我们所有的工作、所有的 PR 都由智能体来创建。

speaker: Drew
en: We focus more on shaping work, so we create issues, uh reviewing work, so we will look at PRs as they're put up.

speaker: Drew
en: Increasingly, we're trying to have agents review more and more of that code, and we only invest in the sort of like high-leverage points.

en: And then where we're doing our software engineering, our observability, our monitoring is in the loops themselves.

speaker: Drew
en: And so oftentimes you're creating loops to monitor loops, or you are creating dashboards to control plane your loops and things like that.

en: So that's been our journey.
